businessProblem: Dollar Shave Club is a new startup with a disruptive product (razors at $1/week) and a $5K marketing budget. The company is competing against Gillette (90% market share, $10B revenue, massive ad spend). What is the go-to-market strategy? How should the marketing budget be allocated? What is the most important first success metric? What happens if it works?

evidence.finding: Gillette dominates with 90% market share and $10B revenue; no major disruptor in razors since Gillette Fusion (2006); market ripe for disruption
Customer pain point clear: target demographic resents high razor prices and retail friction; customers are price-sensitive and convenience-driven

supportingData.target_demo: Young males, internet-native, cost-conscious, impatient with retail
supportingData.decision_making: price-sensitive, convenience-driven, willing to try new brands
supportingData.customer_sentiment: Razors are overpriced, buying process is friction-y
supportingData.awareness: mostly unaware of DTC razor options

evidence.finding: Unit economics support sustainability: razors cost $0.35 each to source; pricing at $1/week yields 60-70% gross margin; target CAC must be low (<$10-15)
Fulfillment model is direct-to-consumer shipping (no retail needed); supply chain lean and on-demand manufacturing ready
Channel timing advantageous: YouTube is emerging as entertainment/discovery channel for young males (2012); social media influence emerging; perfect audience-channel match

supportingData.competitor_weakness: uses expensive traditional media (TV, print, sports)
